cards.title: One reconciliation table: a credit is offered only where it could be for

cards.body:
## Summary
Score every (open invoice, incoming credit) pair once in a new pure `lib/reconcile.ts`, give each pair a standing (best / contested / claimed_elsewhere) from the threshold `isAmbiguous` already owns, and derive the row's `candidate_count`, the card's candidates, `lineSuggestions` and `read_invoice` from that one table.

## Description
One relation, credit-could-settle-invoice, is computed three times today: the row's `candidate_count` and the card's candidates by two invoice-side `candidatesFor` passes (db.ts:91, :182), and the credits strip and `read_credits` by a third, credit-side `lineSuggestions` pass (db.ts:301). Only the credit side knows about ambiguity. So the two halves of the app disagree about the same credit. bl_00072 (TRANSFER FROM IRONWOOD STUDIO, $43,650) scores 99 for LB-2026-0115 and 54 for LB-2026-0057. The credit side calls it unambiguous for 0115. The invoice side still counts it for 0057, which lights 0057 in the 'unmatched' filter, gives it the swarm's '+' glyph, prints '1 unapplied credit could belong here' and puts the credit on 0057's card, where `matchAction` would accept it. That would apply 0115's money to 0057 and leave 0115 overdue and chaseable. bl_00010 does the same to LB-2026-0047 (71 against LB-2026-0015's 99). The new rule offers a credit to an invoice only when that invoice is its best fit or a real contender (within AMBIGUOUS_GAP of the best). The runner-up stays visible on the credit side but is marked claimed_elsewhere, which is what the journey test pins. Every reader reads the one table, so the count, the card and both tools cannot drift. A latent drift goes too: the 5-versus-3 slicing means a credit with four contenders gets a different count from the row than from `read_invoice`. Technique: measurement-honesty / co-published-numbers-must-reconcile (a total and its parts on one screen come from one computation).

## Flow
- `reconcile(open: ScoreInput & {id}[], lines)` -> { byCredit(lineId): ranked offers with standing, ambiguous; byInvoice(id): offered credits (standing != claimed_elsewhere) }. Pure, no server import.
- db.ts: one request-cached `reconciliation()` over `listInvoices` rows plus `unappliedLines()`. `toRow` computes candidate_count from it in a post-pass, which breaks today's listInvoices -> lineSuggestions cycle. `getInvoiceDetail.candidates`, `lineSuggestions` and `unappliedCredits` read it too.
- match.ts exports the contender rule beside isAmbiguous (one threshold, two uses).
- types.ts: `standing` and an optional `claimed_by {invoice_id, number, score}` on LineSuggestion and MatchCandidate.
- BooksTools read_invoice drops offers whose standing is claimed_elsewhere.

## Expected impact
Two seeded invoices stop advertising a credit that belongs to another invoice, and that credit is no longer offered where it would misapply $43,650 or $3,375. The 'unmatched' filter, the glyph, the status sentence, the card and read_invoice all agree by construction. The class closes: the two halves can no longer judge the same credit differently.

## Evaluation
Claim: a credit is offered to an invoice only when it could be for that invoice, and every reader agrees on which invoices those are.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (cases 5 and 7 are guards that are green before and must stay green; on the seed today LB-2026-0057 and LB-2026-0047 each report candidate_count 1 from a credit that scores 28-45 points higher elsewhere, measured by a scratch probe on scratch books)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases
Result: better
Gate: none
cards.evidence: Scratch probe on seeded scratch books (node --test, tempHome): invoices 125, incoming unapplied credits 19; credits offered to more than one invoice: 3 - bl_00118 LB-2026-0901:99 LB-2026-0900:93 (ambiguous, correct); bl_00010 LB-2026-0015:99 LB-2026-0047:71; bl_00072 LB-2026-0115:99 LB-2026-0057:54. 'LB-2026-0057 offered TRANSFER FROM IRONWOOD STUDIO 54 but best is LB-2026-0115 99'; 'LB-2026-0047 offered TRANSFER FROM COPPERLINE INDUSTRIES 71 but best is LB-2026-0015 99'. db.ts:91 `const candidates = takesCredit(...) ? candidatesFor(...)`; db.ts:301 `export const lineSuggestions = cache(...)` re-scores with scoreCandidate; BooksTools.tsx:316 `Object.entries(suggestions).flatMap(...)` for read_invoice.

cards.title: Never chase money already on the statement: the chase names the credit to apply

cards.body:
## Summary
An invoice whose payment is already on the bank statement can't be chased until that credit is applied (or applied elsewhere). The refusal names the credit (memo, amount, date, line id) so the next act is match_bank_line, not a dunning letter. The invoice's status sentence says 'Looks paid' instead of 'never chased'.

## Description
13 of the 52 overdue invoices on the seeded books (25%) have a strong, unambiguous credit on the statement whose best fit is that invoice. Several of those memos quote the invoice number: 'SEPA CR IRONWOOD STUDIO INV LB-2026-0104', $17,775, posted 28 Jun. Today `draft_reminder('LB-2026-0104', 'firm')` drafts 'LB-2026-0104 is now 67 days past due ... or we will pause scheduled work until it clears' to a client who paid 67 days ago, and `send_reminder` sends it. The data that settles the question is already computed for the credits strip (`unappliedCredits`) but never reaches the chase. The README's own act-2 command, 'every invoice over 30 days, draft a chase for each', drafts six such letters (0104, 0100, 0085, 0112, 0115, 0042), and ADR 0147's tray can now do it in one press. The decision is made blind even though the app holds the answer. The rule has no dead end. The block lifts the moment the credit is applied, here or to the invoice it really belongs to, so a person who knows the credit is someone else's matches it there and the chase reopens. An ambiguous credit (the Kestrel retainers) does not block. It turns the draft's answer into a 'check before sending' that names both invoices, the way `isMostlyPaid` already warns. The send re-checks at the last moment, per concurrency-guards / preparation-is-the-staleness-window: a letter drafted before the statement was imported is not sent after it.

## Flow
- lib/db.ts: request-cached `settlingCredits()` -> Map<invoiceId, SettlingCredit> from `unappliedCredits()`: not ambiguous, best fit = the invoice, confidence strong.
- lib/chase.ts (pure): `chaseVerdict(row, settling, contested)` -> null | { block: true, message, settling_credit } | { block: false, warning }.
- app/actions.ts: whyNotChase defers to chaseVerdict on draft and on send. DraftResult and SendResult carry settling_credit.
- lib/lanes/read.ts statusOf takes the settling credit: lateness first (agreeing with the glyph), then 'Looks paid: ... - apply it before chasing.' lib/lanes/index.ts passes it.
- ADR 0149 records the tightened rule.

## Expected impact
No seeded client who has paid can be sent a dunning letter: 6 refused on the README beat, 13 across all overdue invoices. The agent is given the one act that actually closes the item. The card's sentence stops calling a paid invoice 'never chased'.

## Evaluation
Claim: a chase is refused while the statement holds a strong, unambiguous credit for that invoice, the refusal hands over the credit to apply, and an ambiguous or weak credit only warns.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (case 6 is a guard on the new pure function; measured today: 13 of 52 overdue invoices covered by such a credit, 6 of 35 over 30 days, and every one of them drafts and sends)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - the acceptance cases
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
